{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that personal moral standards (PMS) would show positive correlations with moral values, virtues, and judgments, and that concern over moral mistakes (CMM) would show distinct relationships with these variables.",
  "design": "correlational",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Personal moral standards (PMS) and concern over moral mistakes (CMM) measured via an adapted version of the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale.",
  "outcome_measure": "Gratitude judgments (measured via a vignette describing a situation where a peer provides help, followed by items assessing gratitude, indebtedness, and willingness to help).",
  "population_and_setting": "539 university students in the eastern coastal region of the People's Republic of China.",
  "sample_size_total": 539,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited after classes; no compensation provided.",
  "analysis_plan": "Partial correlations between moral perfectionism dimensions (PMS and CMM) and moral outcomes, controlling for the overlap between PMS and CMM.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used three separate samples (N=168, N=206, N=165) to measure different moral outcomes (values, virtues, and judgments). The focal effect concerns the partial correlation between moral perfectionism dimensions and gratitude judgments in Study 3."
}
